title: Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows: Event group chat for organisers and presenters in webinars and structured meetings
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap and preserves Microsoft's conflicting descriptions of chat access for room presenters. The documented policy path and PowerShell command are correct. Minor corrections are needed to cite the Android roadmap comparison and align the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.quote: You can also switch to a separate chat with attendees enabling smooth event experiences for all.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Rooms Windows Event Group chat webinar structured meetings app version enable admin setting'; read Plan for Teams events, meeting-chat, event-chat, XML and Pro portal settings. No enablement step specific to this extension is stated.

claims.quote: In events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, the chat experience differs depending on the event role. Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters can chat with each other in the event group chat.

claims.claim: Learn describes Event group chat as separate from attendee chat.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change and support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn lists chat as unavailable in GCC, GCCH and DoD under meeting-chat limitations for events optimized for large audiences.
claims.quote:
The following limitations apply to meeting chat in events optimized for large audiences:
Chat isn't available on the GCC, GCCH, and DoD government clouds at this time.

claims.claim: Meeting chat is reached in the Teams admin center through Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Meeting chat.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to edit. Go to the Meeting engagement section. Set Meeting chat to your chosen value

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled turns off meeting chat for the assigned policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off meeting chat for users with this assigned policy, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -MeetingChatEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: Meeting chat policy governs whether participants in users' meetings and events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat.
claims.quote:
As an admin, you can control:
Whether participants in your users' meetings and events with up to 1,000 attendees can read and send chat messages.

claims.claim: Meeting chat is a per-user and per-organizer policy.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't apply to channel meetings and is a per-user and per-organizer policy.

claims.claim: The Meeting chat UI value Off corresponds to the PowerShell value Disabled.
claims.quote: | Off | Disabled | Meeting chat is turned off for all participants; organizers can't use their Allow meeting chat to turn on chat in their meetings. Organizers can't override this setting. |

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly establish whether Meeting chat policy governs the new Windows Event Group chat in structured meetings and webinars.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams Rooms Event group MeetingChatEnabledType policy admin' and 'Event group chat admin No control'; read meeting-chat, event-chat, Plan for Teams events and XML settings. Large-audience Event group has 'No control'; the new Windows extension's policy binding is not stated.
